children: CITIC Securities said in a research report that market pricing of inflation is weakening rapidly, while the long-end pricing anchor has shifted toward the growth and AI cycle. According to Odaily, U.S. CPI rose 3.7% year over year in September and PPI increased 6.3%, both above expectations, but the 10-year Treasury yield’s response weakened within 24 hours.

On October 14, after the CPI report, the 10-year yield initially rose about 13 basis points to 5.325%, then retreated and closed lower. After PPI data was released on October 15, the 10-year yield edged up about 2.5 basis points, while the 30-year yield fell; the 10-year yield subsequently dropped to around 5.048%.

The report said the recession risk reflected in long-term pricing is the tail risk of a downturn in the AI capital expenditure cycle, rather than a conventional demand recession, and can coexist with stagflation. It described current pricing as exploratory and said it has not yet confirmed a trend.

CITIC Securities said U.S. stocks could see continued sector rotation in the short term, with capital moving from AI-related themes toward energy, defensive consumer staples and health care, which may benefit from expectations of a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections. It also said Hong Kong stocks could benefit from a reversal in overseas trading of AI hardware and from portfolio adjustments related to the possibility of Indonesia’s removal from the MSCI Emerging Markets Index.

title: CITIC Securities: Inflation Pricing Fades as Long-End Anchor Shifts to Growth and AI
